scope: Direct review of the explicitly selected final RU/EN Booky synthetic large-text captures, covering visible control labels, card header and body framing, character framing and the selected recovery/gesture states. All configured captures are authenticated; only the explicitly selected subset is directly reviewed.
limitations: This visual review covers 10 of 22 final captures. It does not claim all retained images were inspected again.
The enlarged-font browser condition is synthetic and does not establish native OS text scaling or Dynamic Type behavior.

Static images establish only visible framing and text at their captured scroll positions. They cannot establish trusted-touch activation, focus, scrolling reachability, persistence, recovery readback or source-state preservation; those claims depend on the corresponding formal browser assertions.
No universal absence of overlap, installed-device, nonzero OS safe-area or iOS acceptance is claimed.

findings: The full localized Booky name, Stop and Close fit in the compact header.
The visible body copy stays inside the card; lower content continues in its scroll region.
The full enlarged localized name fits on its own title row; Stop and Close occupy a separate row with contained labels.
Enlarged body copy extends below the visible scroll region; this static frame does not by itself establish scrolling reachability.
The enlarged disabled walking label wraps inside the expanded button border rather than spilling below it.
The separate movement and hide controls and the character remain visible in the captured viewport.
The localized title remains readable in the short landscape card; Stop and Close are fully visible with contained labels.
The help body is only partly visible below the sticky header and continues in a scroll region; the static view is not a full-content accessibility claim.
The complete localized Replace with calm movements label fits inside its visible recovery button.
The expanded title and header actions remain visible while the recovery button is fully exposed at this scroll position.
